papers.title: Pangenome Discoveries from Clinical Long-Read Genomes in Underrepresented Populations with Neurodevelopmental Disorders
papers.abstract: Genetic diagnoses remain elusive for many individuals with neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs), and the gap is wider in populations poorly represented in genomic reference resources. To demonstrate the equitable advantage of long-read whole genome sequencing (LR-WGS) and pangenomes in terms of clinical utility, we analyzed 211 NDD cases and 107 unaffected relatives from 24 populations, integrating their assemblies, resulting in a total of 1204 haplotypes with the Human Pangenome Reference Consortium Release 2 (HPRC_r2) and the Arab Pangenome Reference (APR) datasets. Clinical interpretation of small variants and structural variants (SVs) revealed pathogenic or likely pathogenic findings in 38.9% of the cases (82/211), and our workflow further detected pathogenic repeat expansions in 3.8% of the cases and runs of homozygosity (ROHs) exceeding 300 Mb in 4.7% of the cases, revealing substantial autozygosity suggestive of strong inbreeding. Beyond these clinical assessments, pangenome analysis revealed 3.9 million population-level novel small variants, 39,782 SVs and an average of 2.17 Mb of novel sequence per individual absent from linear references and global pangenomes. We identified 85.9 kb of case-unique nonreference sequences in exonic segments overlapping with curated NDD gene sets. Graph-based tertiary analysis further identified rare exonic complex homozygous rearrangements in the NDD associated genes for 2.4% of the cases. Together, these findings emphasize how diverse genome assemblies extend variant discovery beyond established linear reference-based clinical interpretation.

papers.title: Male-specific genome sequences for non-invasive sex identification in Nishikigoi (Cyprinus carpio)
papers.abstract: Nishikigoi, ornamental cultivars of the common carp (Cyprinus carpio), are economically valuable aquaculture teleosts in which mature females command significantly higher market prices due to superior body conformation and coloration. Consequently, early and non-invasive sex identification is highly desirable for commercial breeding. Although sex determination in common carp follows an XX/XY system, sex-chromosome-specific markers and field-applicable diagnostic methods for Nishikigoi have remained limited. In this study, we conducted sequence-based bulked segregant analysis using whole-genome shotgun sequencing of female and male pools in Kohaku, a representative Nishikigoi lineage. We identified male-specific candidate contigs and successfully developed PCR-based male-specific markers. Validation across multiple Nishikigoi varieties and wild common carp demonstrated that primary primer pairs achieved high diagnostic accuracy. Comparative genomic analysis revealed that these candidate contigs mapped to the genomic region on chromosome 25B containing the male-determining gene Pangu, with the primary marker located in immediate physical proximity to the gene. To enable field diagnostics, we combined non-invasive epidermal mucus DNA extraction, loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP), and chromatography-printed array strip (C-PAS) technology, establishing a rapid on-site detection workflow. Overall, this study provides highly reliable PCR markers associated with the sex-determination locus and establishes a non-invasive, field-applicable diagnostic platform to streamline commercial Nishikigoi breeding and sex-selected stock management.

papers.title: Integrated exome-transcriptome analysis of a schizophrenia case with an exceptionally low polygenic risk score
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia liability reflects both common polygenic variation and rarer variants of larger effect. We investigated a post-mortem schizophrenia case (SZ07) with a schizophrenia polygenic risk score below the first percentile among ancestry-matched cases, asking whether individual-level genomic and transcriptomic analyses could help identify potentially novel schizophrenia-relevant variants. We used exome analysis with multiple variant-prediction tools to generate a panel of variants and corresponding candidate genes potentially implicated in the pathological process in SZ07. The prioritised variants were then assessed using RNA sequencing of three cortical regions. Of these, only an IZUMO4 splice-acceptor variant showed direct RNA-level support. Beyond variant-specific analyses, we characterised broader transcriptomic abnormalities in the SZ07 brain. Pathway analysis of gene-level expression deviations implicated innate immune processes, calcium signalling, synaptic biology, and axon remodelling. Notably, compared with conventional single-sample biological pathway analysis, the analysis we used showed only a weak association with neuronal specificity, suggesting their reduced sensitivity to the main axis of variation related to cellular composition in bulk brain tissue gene expression data. Although the candidate genes showed no significant pathway-level convergence, the broader transcriptomic profile revealed coherent biological alterations largely compatible with the documented history of cerebrovascular disease in SZ07. These results demonstrate how the integration of exome and transcriptome data at the individual level enables the formulation and constraint of hypotheses regarding patient-specific genetic features and their molecular consequences, while highlighting important limitations related to tissue composition, comorbidity, and the choice of reference cohort.

papers.title: A genetic screen to identify host factors required for commensal bacterial adherence to the gut epithelia
papers.abstract: Bacterial adherence to gut epithelial cells likely involves host genetic components. We isolated a gut commensal bacterium, Lelliottia jeotgali, that can robustly colonize C. elegans through attachment to intestinal epithelial cells. Here, we developed a novel screen in C. elegans to identify host genes required for microbiome bacterial colonization. Using transgenic L. jeotgali strain expressing tdTomato, we conducted forward genetic screens in C. elegans to select for mutants that completely lost colonization. We identified multiple allelic mutations in five different C. elegans genes, termed knockout of Lelliottia adherence (kola) mutants, with a near complete loss of adherence. Each of kola-1-5 is uncharacterized and predicted to encode for a secreted or membrane-bound protein. We also identified gly-5, a GalNAc transferase that initiates O-linked glycosylation. Overall, we describe the first C. elegans screen to identify host factors that control microbiome bacterial colonization in the gut.

papers.title: Deciphering the Dynamics of Leukemogenic Transformation from Clonal Hematopoiesis in Congenital Neutropenia
papers.abstract: Inherited neutropenia syndromes, severe congenital neutropenia (CN) and Shwachman-Diamond syndrome (SDS), confer a high cumulative risk of MDS and AML. It is not yet clear which somatic mutations, in which combination, allele frequency and sequence identify patients at high risk. We analyzed clonal hematopoiesis (CH) in the largest representative cohort of inherited neutropenia patients to date - 658 samples from 309 patients - using error-corrected panel sequencing with longitudinal sampling. This was complemented in selected cases by single-cell DNA sequencing and genotyping of single-cell derived colonies. CH was detected in early childhood, affecting 37.7% of CN and 60% of SDS patients. The somatic mutation burden remained essentially unchanged over decades. In CN, CSF3R mutations were dominant across genetic subtypes, while additional mutations were rare and included ASXL1, TET2, and DNMT3A. ASXL1 mutations most frequently co-occurred with CSF3R mutations. Co-occurring CSF3R and TP53 mutations were only found in SRP54-CN and CLPB-CN patients. In SDS, TP53 was the most frequently mutated gene, followed by low-prevalence somatic mutations in DNMT3A, IDH1, PTPN11, and RUNX1. In CN-MDS/AML, RUNX1 and SETBP1 mutations emerged shortly before progression to MDS/AML, and membrane-proximal CSF3R mutations only at the leukemic stage. In SDS, biallelic TP53-mutant clones expanded prior to transformation, and a variant allele frequency (VAF) of dominant TP53 clone above 0.074 discriminated between patients who progressed and those who did not. Peripheral blood reflected bone marrow genotype for most key drivers. Leukemic transformation in inherited neutropenia is therefore not stochastic, but rather follows a defined mutational sequence, initiated in childhood.

papers.title: Regulation of sociality and neuronal development by the translation initiation factor eIF4H1 in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Most animal species exhibit some level of sociality. However, whether sociality-related traits evolved independently, or are instead derived from common core mechanisms, remains controversial. Nevertheless, an emerging theoretical framework stipulates that key aspects of how animals interact with their social environments may be regulated by a phylogenetically conserved genetic toolkit. Therefore, we hypothesized that mutations that lead to social deficits in specific human disorders may implicate genes that play conserved roles in the regulation of core social traits across Animalia. Specifically, here we focus on genes associated with Williams syndrome (WS), a rare human multi-system disorder characterized in part by hypersocial cognitive traits. WS is caused by a hemizygous chromosomal microdeletion of 25-28 protein-coding genes. Consequently, it has been hypothesized that haploinsufficiency in at least one of these genes plays an important role in the development and/or function of social neural circuits in humans. Because the Drosophila genome encodes orthologs of 17 of the 28 genes deleted in WS, we reasoned that at least some of them may serve a conserved role in the regulation of social traits across flies and humans, as predicted by the genetic toolkit framework. Using a neuron-specific RNAi knockdown screen, we identified eIF4H1, an ortholog of a highly conserved subunit of the eukaryotic translation initiation complex eIF4F, as a candidate gene for neuronal regulation of sociality in the fly. We show that eIF4H1 expression is predominantly neuronal in the adult fly brain, and that its action plays a differential role in the organization of specific dopaminergic neuron subtypes that are associated with sociality and cognitive functions. These results indicate that eIF4H1 may serve a conserved function in regulating the development of the neuronal circuits that regulate social behaviors, thus supporting the idea of a conserved sociality genetic toolkit.

papers.title: Overlapping enhancer activity robustly regulates rax expression during ocular development in zebrafish
papers.abstract: Vertebrate eye development relies on the tightly regulated yet highly dynamic spatiotemporal expression of eye field transcription factors that coordinate developmental programs required for the formation of a functional eye. The gene rax is among the earliest expressed eye field transcription factors and is specifically associated with ocular-fated tissue. It encodes a transcription factor that is essential for optic vesicle evagination, the precursor to the optic cup and retina. Although the developmental functions of rax are well characterized, the cis-regulatory elements that control its expression remain poorly understood. Using zebrafish (Danio rerio), I identified five novel ocular enhancers and demonstrate that they drive similar spatiotemporal expression patterns as rax at three key stages of eye development. Furthermore, I performed an in-depth characterization of two enhancers and demonstrate that they exhibit substantial transcript-level overlap with endogenous rax expression during development. Additionally, through the generation of enhancer deletion lines, I further demonstrate that the gene regulatory network (GRN) controlling rax expression is largely robust to individual and combinatorial enhancer perturbations. However, perturbation of this regulatory network can result in rax-associated ocular abnormalities, including microphthalmia and anophthalmia. Together, these findings highlight the importance of studying developmental ocular enhancers to better understand the functions of noncoding genomic regions and provide insight into potential causes of unexplained congenital eye disease.

papers.title: Quantitative trait loci mapping identifies genetic loci modifying MafAS64F-mediated dysglycemia
papers.abstract: Increasing evidence has shown the role of genetic background on the penetrance of monogenic diabetes. A missense mutation of the pancreatic {beta}-cell-enriched transcription factor MafA co-segregates with diabetes (MafA-MODY) and non-syndromic insulinomatosis. We recently investigated the effects of genetic background on MafAS64F-driven dysglycemia in genetically diverse mice harboring this mutation. Here we leveraged the effects of genetic background on phenotypic penetrance to map quantitative trait loci (QTL) potentially modifying glycemia in response to this variant. We investigated MafaS64F/+ mice from an F2 intercross of the C57BL/6J and SJL/J genetic backgrounds through oral glucose tolerance testing at 4, 5, 6, and 8 weeks of age to evaluate glucose tolerance and glycemic trajectory. All F2 mice were genetically monitored for single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) between the C57BL/6J and SJL/J backgrounds, allowing us to identify modifying loci on 6 chromosomes (2, 126 Mbp; 3, 59 Mbp and 103 Mbp; 7, 47 Mbp; 11 45 Mbp; 13, 4 Mbp; and 16, 85-97 Mbp), containing 172 candidate genes. For example, known MODY genes Abcc8 (Sur1) and Kcnj11 (Kir6.2) are within the QTL region on chromosome 7 and contain polymorphisms between backgrounds that may impart combinatorial effects on the phenotypic penetrance of MafAS64F-mediated dysglycemia

papers.title: Genomic signatures of long-term selection in the Langhill dairy herd: the power of a five-decade experiment for sustainable dairy cattle breeding
papers.abstract: Background Selective breeding has transformed dairy cattle productivity, but the genomic consequences of long-term directional selection - what it costs in diversity and where in the genome it acts - are hard to quantify because contemporaneous control populations are rare. The Langhill experiment, established in 1973, is one of the world's longest-running dairy cattle selection trials with a designed control line kept under common management. We used this resource population to ask what five decades of bull selection have cost in genetic diversity, where in the genome selection has acted, and whether complementary scans converge on the loci under selection. Results We genotyped archived blood samples from 1,126 cows of two genetic lines: a Select line sired by bulls in the top decile of UK genetic merit for milk fat-plus-protein yield, and a Control line sired by bulls of average merit. The Select line showed the expected gains in every yield trait. Inbreeding accumulated at the same annual rate in both lines, and effective population size, estimated from that rate, was approximately 33. Linkage disequilibrium was higher in the Select line at every marker distance from 2 to 300 kb. Autozygosity was 24.7% higher in the Select line than in the Control line (0.078 versus 0.063), a difference robust across four calling parameter sets and two independent callers. The excess was confined to runs of homozygosity longer than 2 Mb; shorter runs did not differ between lines, confirming a shared founder base and placing all divergence after the lines were split. It did not arise from a numerically narrower sire pool: the Select line used more sires (79 versus 72), each with fewer daughters, yet its cows were three times more related to one another. Twenty-eight regions across thirteen chromosomes showed strong differentiation; intersecting five scans identified a four-method signal on chromosome 21 spanning the SERPINA gene cluster and sixteen three-method regions, including chromosome 3, with haplotype and diversity statistics agreeing on the line carrying the signal in fourteen of seventeen. Autozygosity itself did not localise to any region. Conclusions Selection left two genomic footprints: diffuse, recent inbreeding accumulated through the narrow ancestry of the elite sire pool, and localised differentiation at specific loci. Runs of homozygosity index only the first process; the second is captured by frequency- and haplotype-based differentiation scans. Because the cost of inbreeding is incurred through ancestry rather than the number of bulls used, mating schemes that constrain the rate of co-ancestry would be preferable to simply managing the number of sires selected and used.

papers.title: A largely shared genetic architecture underlies Saccharomyces cerevisiae persistence across different mouse host genotypes
papers.abstract: The extent to which interactions between microbial and host genotypes shape opportunistic pathogen persistence within hosts is an important open question. To assess the contribution of these interactions to persistence, we used Saccharomyces cerevisiae , a genetically tractable model for studying opportunistic fungal persistence in mammalian hosts. A pooled panel of barcoded haploid segregants from a cross between a laboratory strain and a clinical isolate, together with both parents, was introduced intravenously into seven genetically diverse mouse strains. We measured the relative persistence of segregants in mouse brains and livers using barcode sequencing. Persistence showed transgressive segregation in both organs. On average across the two organs, yeast genotype explained 45.2% of the variance in segregant persistence, whereas yeast genotype-by-host genotype interactions explained only 2.9%. Linkage mapping showed that loci detected in more host genotypes generally explained more phenotypic variance than those detected in fewer host genotypes. At some loci, genetic variation correlated with increased yeast persistence across multiple organs (general loci) while at others increased persistence in one organ came at the cost of decreased persistence in another (antagonistic loci). General loci contributed disproportionately to brain persistence, whereas liver persistence reflected contributions from both classes. The clinical parent showed greater persistence than the laboratory parent in every host-organ combination, and the additive effects of detected loci predicted the direction of this advantage. Overall, this work shows that in this system, relative microbial persistence is polygenic, with a strong additive component and only a very small contribution from microbial genotype-by-host genotype interactions.

papers.title: Host control and regulation of human anellovirus persistence
papers.abstract: Anelloviruses are the most abundant and diverse eukaryotic viruses known to infect humans and can persist throughout our lifetimes. Despite their ubiquity, the host factors governing their physiologic distribution and abundance remain poorly understood. Here, we construct a viral pangenome of 2,023 strains to quantify anellovirus DNA in >1.1 million participants spanning three genetic biobanks. Genome-wide association studies identify 121 loci linked to viral persistence, predominantly via immune regulation by NF-kB signaling. Further, we associate variable anellovirus detection with conditions characterized by immune dysfunction, including lymphoid malignancies. By screening 3.2 petabases of human single-cell sequencing data, we identify myeloid progenitors in the bone marrow as a prominent site of anellovirus transcription in vivo. Finally, Perturb-seq of anellovirus proteins reveals that anellovirus ORF2, particularly from Alphatorquevirus, attenuates TNF-a-induced NF-kB signaling, connecting host genetic variation, cellular context, and viral immunomodulation to characterize the persistence of the eukaryotic human virome's most abundant component.

papers.title: Analysis of reproductive traits associated with lipoprotein(a) deficiency in participants from the Pakistan Genome Resource
papers.abstract: Aims. Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined, independent risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, driving development of LPA-targeting therapies that markedly lower circulating Lp(a). Because LPA?the gene encoding apolipoprotein(a)?is absent in most model organisms, preclinical studies have limited value for assessing effects such as reproductive safety. Therefore, naturally occurring human LPA ?knockouts? were analyzed to evaluate reproductive outcomes of on-target Lp(a) lowering. Methods and Results. Individuals carrying high-confidence LPA loss-of-function (LoF) variants which reduce Lp(a) in a gene-dosage?dependent manner within the Pakistan Genome Resource were identified. LoF variants showed no depletion of homozygotes relative to Hardy?Weinberg expectations. LPA LoF associations with fertility-related traits (ever having a child and number of children) under additive and recessive models were assessed using regenie-based burden testing, including sex-stratified analyses, and no significant associations were observed. A recall-by-genotype study of female LoF homozygotes alongside heterozygous and non-carrier family member controls was performed, surveying reproductive histories and offspring outcomes. Across 107 pregnancies and 87 children in 19 homozygous LoF women, rates of miscarriage, maternal complications (including preeclampsia, hypertension, and gestational diabetes), delivery complications, neonatal intensive care admission, birth defects, and child health problems were comparable across genotypes with no statistically significant genotype?outcome associations. Conclusions. These genetic and by-genotype analyses indicate that complete lifelong LPA deficiency due to high-confidence LPA loss-of-function variants is not associated with overt adverse maternal fertility, pregnancy or child health outcomes. These findings offer human genetic reassurance regarding reproductive and developmental safety in the context of sustained Lp(a)-lowering, with implications for long-term therapies targeting Lp(a).

papers.title: SARDINE unlocks EWAS summary statistics for large-scale epigenetic biomarker analysis
papers.abstract: Epigenetic clocks are increasingly used to study biological aging, yet their interpretation and utility remain uncertain. Meanwhile, the growing wealth of epigenome-wide association study (EWAS) summary statistics remains largely untapped for evaluating these biomarkers. Here, we introduce SARDINE, a statistical framework that estimates epigenetic clock-phenotype associations using EWAS summary statistics, clock weights, and reference methylation covariance, without individual-level data. SARDINE accurately reproduced individual-level association estimates across 38 epigenetic biomarkers and four phenotypes in 15,677 individuals. Applying SARDINE to diverse EWAS datasets revealed substantial heterogeneity in biomarker associations with aging, diseases, and lifestyle factors. By transforming CpG-level EWAS results into interpretable biomarker-level associations, SARDINE unlocks a largely underutilized data resource and establishes a scalable paradigm for systematic biomarker evaluation and discovery in aging research.

papers.title: Tools for genetic mapping and gene identification in Caenorhabditis briggsae
papers.abstract: The nematode Caenorhabditis briggsae serves as an important companion species for Caenorhabditis elegans for comparative studies. Because C. briggsae exhibits androdioecious reproduction and ease of laboratory culture similar to C. elegans, it has long been used for genetic studies in cross-species comparisons of mutant phenotypes to uncover the evolution of gene function. Here, we provide an updated toolkit for C. briggsae genetic experiments, leveraging the resource of recently improved C. briggsae genome sequence assemblies with variant mapping tools and gene identification methods. We identify and validate a set of indel variants between CGC2 (AF16) and two divergent strains, HK104 and VX34. We then use these variants to genetically map 10 previously isolated mutations and identify the impacted genes using high-throughput sequencing. We combine these new genes with others curated from the literature into an updated map with 73 genes, providing an enriched resource for C. briggsae genetic studies.

papers.title: Genomic and Epigenomic Relationships Capture Different Patterns of Genotype-by-Environment Interaction in Grapevine Clones
papers.abstract: Genotype-by-environment interaction (GEI) challenges selection in clonally propagated perennial crops by reducing the consistency of clone performance across years. In perennial crops, both genetic and epigenetic variation are likely to contribute to complex trait variation among clones. However, the extent to which each molecular source contribute to GEI remains poorly understood. Here, we used UMR-seq, an assay that recovers SNPs and unmethylated-region (UMR; DNA methylation) profiles from a single library, to generate paired genomic and epigenomic profiles for 206 Riesling (Vitis vinifera L.) clones phenotyped for yield and juice quality traits across nine growing seasons. We then partitioned the contribution of each omic layer to clonal variation and GEI, and examined the genomic distribution of their effects. In models without explicit GEI, environmental and residual effects were the largest source of phenotypic variance and the clonal main effect was modest. Genomic relationships accounted for most of the clonal variance in four of five traits, and adding an epigenomic relationship matrix (ERM) to the genomic relationship matrix (GRM) had little effect. In contrast, when GEI effects were modelled using factor-analytic covariance structures, the epigenomic layer captured a substantial proportion of GEI variance and exceeded the genomic contribution in four of five traits. The two omic layers differed not only in the amount of GEI captured, but also in the pattern of clone re-ranking across years. When back-solved effects were aggregated into genomic windows, the largest genomic and epigenomic effects tended to fall in different regions, with overlap no greater than expected by chance. Together, these results show that genomic and epigenomic relationships capture complementary components of year-to-year variation in clone performance, with the epigenomic contribution expressed primarily through GEI. These findings provide a basis for investigating the molecular drivers of GEI and for testing whether genomic and epigenomic information can inform selection for stable clonal performance across variable environments.

papers.title: Deep transcriptomic analysis of molecular mediators of complex traits in heterogeneous stock (HS) rats
papers.abstract: Rats are a powerful model organism for genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of physiological and behavioral traits. Heterogeneous Stock (HS) rats, which were created by intercrossing 8 inbred rat strains, are heavily used for this purpose because of their genetic diversity and accumulated recombinations due to over 100 generations of outbreeding, which improves mapping precision. However, functional genomics resources for post-GWAS interpretation of genomic findings have been limited. We processed 3,160 RNA-seq samples, 1,932 of which were previously unpublished, from 13 tissues as part of RatGTEx. We used Pantry to quantify six modalities of transcriptome regulation (expression, isoform ratio, intron excision ratio, alternative transcription start site (TSS), alternative poly(A), and RNA stability) in each sample, which allowed us to identify 144,876 independent quantitative trait loci (QTL) for 22,599 genes. We performed a transcriptome-wide association study (TWAS) with 19,796 unique genes across tissues and transcriptional modalities and 308 traits collected from 14 studies using FUSION, which identified 7,473 significant gene-trait associations. This work presents a significant expansion of the RatGTEx resource in terms of samples, modes of transcriptome regulation, and genetic analyses. Our findings provide molecular evidence for the involvement of specific genes in mediating GWAS signals through a range of transcriptome regulatory mechanisms. These gene-to-phenotype relationships can be easily applied to genetic analyses in humans and other species. Further experiments can use this evidence to confirm these molecular mediators and target them for the treatment of behavioral and physiological traits and disorders. To facilitate use of these results, we have updated results on RatGTEx.org and provided a new interactive TWAS web portal (twas.ratgtex.org).

papers.title: Transportability of mouse gene knockout models to human complex phenotypes
papers.abstract: Mouse gene knockout studies are a valuable resource for understanding human gene function and the mechanisms underlying disease. However, translating insights to humans requires causal similarities between mouse and human phenotypes. A mouse model is transportable if gene perturbations that impact the mouse phenotype also affect (in orthologous genes) the corresponding human phenotype of interest, with consistent directionality. To assess the transportability of mouse models to human complex traits we combined laboratory mouse gene perturbation data from the high-throughput International Mouse Phenotyping Consortium with predicted loss-of-function data from the UK Biobank within the Gene Perturbation Analysis for Transportability (GPAT) framework. Applying GPAT to 30 matched mouse-human phenotype pairs, we found evidence of transportability for 12 mouse phenotypes including biochemical (e.g. total cholesterol), cellular (e.g. lymphocyte counts) and anthropometric (e.g. length/height) phenotypes. In contrast, there was limited evidence for others such as fat mass and body mass index in the context of the murine experimental conditions. We also found some evidence of transportability of mouse glucose measurements to diabetes mellitus in humans. Genome-wide perturbation effects on matched phenotypes were on average positively correlated between mice and humans (meta-analysis GPAT P = 2.3x10-27). However, the degree of correlation was generally modest and heterogeneous across phenotypes with some gene perturbations strongly associated in both species in opposite directions. Our framework illustrates how perturbation data can be used to quantitatively validate experimental models for understanding human disease aetiology and highlights the need for a range of orthogonal model systems, which may include challenges and perturbations to the mouse knockouts, to interrogate the mechanistic basis of human genetic associations.

papers.title: Short-read whole-genome sequencing identifies the Tg(Tal1-cre/ERT)42-056Jrg transgene insertion site on mouse chromosome 4
papers.abstract: Tg(Tal1-cre/ERT)42-056Jrg, also known as HSC-Scl-CreERT, is a well-used transgenic allele that enables genetic manipulation in mouse hematopoietic cells. Using short-read whole-genome sequencing, we identified the transgene insertion site on chromosome 4 approximately 6 kb upstream of Echdc2.

papers.title: LRCQ: phenome-wide heritability enrichment of genomic loci from GWAS summary statistics
papers.abstract: Some genetic variants are associated with many traits, but a variant's GWAS statistics are also inflated by the effects of variants in LD with it and by confounding shared by all variants in a study. Existing measures of per-variant pleiotropy, such as counts of significant associations or multi-trait association tests, do not separate these sources. Stratified LD score regression separates them for one trait at a time and only through predefined annotations. We present LRCQ (LD score regression on {chi}2 across many GWAS), which estimates for each locus its phenome-wide heritability enrichment: the variance of its causal effects across a set of traits, relative to an average locus. LRCQ regresses squared Z-scores from 30 or more GWAS jointly on squared LD, with per-trait LDSC intercepts and heritabilities fitted in earlier stages. Its pooled least-squares solution has a closed form whose cost does not grow with the number of traits. Its standard errors account for sample overlap and genetic correlation between GWAS. Squared Z-scores identify enrichment at the resolution of LD clumps, not single SNPs, so LRCQ reports clump-level estimates ("omni-loci"). These estimates can be aggregated over any functional annotation or gene set chosen after the analysis. In simulations with real UK Biobank LD and 30 to 1,000 traits, LRCQ was unbiased for its clump-level estimand. When GWAS share samples its test statistics are strongly right-skewed: normal-reference p-values were up to 10-fold anti-conservative at P < 0.001, and skewness-corrected p-values from the exact third cumulant restored type-I error and FDR control. Model-based standard errors were calibrated once the enrichment estimates plugged into them kept the polygenic background. It ranked enriched loci better than mean {chi}2, LD-normalised {chi}2, multi-trait omnibus tests and significant-association counts in 13 of 16 scenarios. Its main vulnerability was a misspecified LDSC intercept. Applied to 444 Pan-UK Biobank European-ancestry GWAS, LRCQ found strongly non-uniform phenome-wide enrichment: the SD of true clump-mean enrichment was 8.3, against a genome mean of 1. It identified 70 omni-loci (99 LD clumps) at FDR 5%, including CRP, CETP, APOB, AKTIP, SMOX, the SHBG region, CASZ1 and HNF1A. These ranked only moderately with mean {chi}2 and poorly with counts of significant associations. Gene-level phenome-wide enrichment rose with loss-of-function constraint. Phenome-wide heritability was 3-5-fold enriched in coding, conserved, 5' UTR and promoter sequence, and depleted in repressed chromatin. LRCQ turns hundreds of biobank GWAS into an LD-corrected map of where phenome-wide genetic variance lies, and complements its companion method LRCP, which estimates genetic-effect correlations between loci.

papers.title: Deep Recovery of Effective Migration Surfaces
papers.abstract: The isolation-by-distance (IBD) principle describes the tendency for genetic relatedness to decline with geographic distance. Although the existence IBD has long been documented in natural populations, recent analyses of spatially referenced genotype data have shown that the strength of this relationship can vary across a landscape due to geographic barriers, habitat compatibility, or other factors. Effective migration surfaces (EMS) have emerged as a popular exploratory tool for visualizing spatial patterns in IBD. However, fitting likelihood-based EMS models is often computationally demanding, requiring repeated large-scale matrix calculations. Here, we introduce Deep Recovery of Effective Migration Surfaces (dreems), a graph neural network for amortized inference of effective migration surfaces. dreems maps genetic covariance and sampling locations directly to an effective migration surface, while simultaneously providing predictive uncertainty estimates. Once trained, the network accommodates different graph sizes and sampling designs without needing to re-train. Across independent coalescent simulations that were not seen during training, dreems has roughly 10-30% lower estimation error compared to a state-of-the-art likelihood-based method, with the largest gains observed under sparse sampling designs that are commonly encountered in practice. Reanalysis of several published datasets recovers spatial patterns that are broadly consistent with earlier likelihood-based estimates, while reducing computation time by orders of magnitude.

papers.title: SeverYX: An ensemble framework for robust variant severity classification
papers.abstract: Accurate interpretation of genetic variants in clinical genomics depends on reconciling multiple computational predictors that often disagree or provide incomplete evidence. We present SeverYX, a transparent, rule-based ensemble framework that consolidates conservation, splicing, and functional-impact predictors into a three-tier severity classification ('High', 'Medium', 'Low') through an effect-aware decision architecture. We benchmarked SeverYX against a curated ClinVar dataset of 270,208 MANE-transcript variants (86,161 pathogenic/likely pathogenic, 184,047 benign/likely benign), stratified by molecular consequence, review status, and haploinsufficiency. The baseline configuration achieved 97.6% concordance with ClinVar; at a fixed High cut, 90.0% of pathogenic and 2.0% of benign variants were assigned High. Concordance was highest for loss-of-function variants and lowest for non-coding and unclassified pathogenic variants, reflecting known gaps in current predictive tools. Systematic threshold optimization, combined with the addition of AlphaMissense and REVEL as missense predictors, raised overall concordance to 98.7%, reduced the benign High rate to 0.4% (at a cost of pathogenic High sensitivity falling to 88.3%), and improved the Matthews correlation coefficient from 0.895 to 0.908. These results show that SeverYX offers a transparent, reproducible and extensible approach for consolidating heterogeneous variant-effect evidence into clinically interpretable severity calls, and a scalable path for incorporating future predictive models into genomic interpretation workflows.

papers.title: LRCP: identifying functionally related SNPs and genes from phenome-wide genetic-effect correlations using GWAS summary statistics
papers.abstract: Genetic correlation describes which traits share genetic causes. The transposed question, which variants act alike across the phenome, has no comparable estimator, although it points directly to shared genes, pathways and regulators. Correlations of GWAS Z scores between variants across many traits are easy to compute, but they are confounded by linkage disequilibrium (LD) and, for any pair of variants, by sample overlap and genetic correlation among the GWAS. We show that in 452 Pan-UK Biobank GWAS the effective number of independent traits is only 58, and that naive tests reject 51-70% of null pairs of distal variants. We introduce LRCP (likelihood and regression on cross-products of Z scores), which estimates the phenome-wide genetic-effect correlation{rho} between SNPs by regressing Z-score cross-products on LD cross components, using per-SNP heritability enrichment from the companion method LRCQ and LDSC-derived plug-ins. For variants in different LD blocks the estimator has a closed form, and its standard errors account exactly for the dependence among GWAS. In simulations LRCP is unbiased (absolute bias at most 0.03), its 95% intervals cover 93-98%, and its type-I error is 5.0-5.7%, whereas naive correlations are attenuated by 41-64% and reject up to 51% of null pairs. In Pan-UK Biobank, LRCP recovers the expected signs among PCSK9, LDLR and APOB variants and estimates{rho} = 0.90 between the TP53 polyadenylation variant rs78378222 and MDM2 rs3730556, whose Z scores correlate at r = 0.67 across traits (conditional bootstrap P = 0.015), although this correlation lies along a shared body-size and red-cell trait axis. Single variant pairs are near the resolution of current biobanks, with precision limited by the number of genetically distinct traits. Genome-wide, among 7,793 enriched LD clumps (30.2 million distal pairs), a conditional test finds 17 pairs at FDR 5%, where naive correlation flags 23 million. Simulating the whole screen under the null shows that this test is conservative and that the 113 strongest links (P < 10-5) lie far beyond the null, which yields 0.025 such pairs per screen. Linked genes share Reactome pathways 4.9 times more often than random pairs of enriched loci. The top pairs form 19 modules, the largest of which match known biology: myeloid differentiation (IRF8, CEBPE, IKZF1), LDL and HDL metabolism, iron homeostasis (TMPRSS6, TFRC), the red-cell membrane (SPTA1, ANK1) and type-2 immunity (TSLP, IL13). LRCP turns phenome-wide summary statistics into a map of functionally related variants and genes.

papers.title: A DNM1L GTPase Effector Domain Deletion Causes Intermediate Defects in Peroxisomal and Mitochondrial Dynamics and Reveals a Targetable Metabolic Vulnerability
papers.abstract: DNM1L encodes dynamin-related protein 1 (DRP1), a key GTPase regulating mitochondrial and peroxisomal dynamics. Pathogenic DNM1L variants are associated with a broad spectrum of neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disorders, with phenotypic severity varying by affected protein domain. While variants in the GTPase domain are typically associated with milder phenotypes and middle-domain variants with severe developmental and epileptic encephalopathy, the functional impact of GTPase effector domain (GED) variants remains less defined. Here, we describe four individuals harboring a recurrent heterozygous GED deletion (L700del) presenting with movement disorders and lacking severe infantile encephalopathy, consistent with an intermediate clinical phenotype. Patient-derived fibroblasts exhibited tubular peroxisomes and enlarged mitochondria, while Drosophila models demonstrated that DNM1LL700del has intermediate functional effects that were more pronounced than those of a GTPase-domain variant A192E but less severe than those of the middle-domain variant G350R. Comparison with another GED variant, Y691C, further demonstrated variant-specific differences in severity within the GED. Metabolic stress assays showed that L700del fibroblasts exhibited impaired growth under galactose conditions, consistent with increased vulnerability under conditions dependent on mitochondrial oxidative metabolism. Bezafibrate, a PPAR agonist that promotes mitochondrial biogenesis, partially rescued this growth defect. Together, these findings support a functional allelic spectrum in DNM1L-associated disease in which protein domain contributes to, but does not completely determine, functional severity. L700del represents an intermediate-strength allele associated with a movement-disorder phenotype and a pharmacologically modifiable metabolic vulnerability.

papers.title: Linking dynamic photosynthetic traits to biomass: a functional data framework that pinpoints when photosynthesis limits growth
papers.abstract: Photosynthesis responds rapidly to environmental changes, such as light fluctuations, and these responses affect how much carbon plants gain over time. Modelling genetic variation in photosynthesis over time opens a route for selection on photosynthetic performance. High-throughput chlorophyll fluorescence has enabled measurements of photosynthetic processes at high time resolution, yet methods to model the temporal and genetic variation in these time-series data remain scarce. Here, we combined splines and functional principal component analysis (FPCA) to model genotype-specific trajectories of fluorescence traits and capture their main variation in a few components. We applied this approach to 412 Arabidopsis thaliana MAGIC lines under daily sinusoidal and fluctuating light. The first component captured differences in overall trait level, whereas subsequent components captured differences in how trait values changed across days, mainly in the early growing period. These component scores predicted final dry weight reasonably well (average r = 0.7224 under sinusoidal and 0.82 under fluctuating light). Information on changes across days added most predictive value when measurements were limited to a few days. Time-varying coefficients revealed that the associations between fluorescence traits and dry weight changed over time. For most traits, these associations were strongest early in the growing period. Our framework thus shows not only which photosynthetic processes are associated with biomass, but also when. This insight will point to the period in which photosynthesis limits growth and to the traits beneficial to select for.

papers.title: The role of the fruitless P3 transcript in development in Drosophila melanogaster
papers.abstract: The generation of multiple transcripts from a single gene through alternative promoter usage and alternative splicing is a major source of functional diversity in eukaryotic genomes. The fruitless (fru) gene of Drosophila melanogaster is a classic example of transcript complexity, producing at least 15 transcript isoforms through the use of alternative promoters and terminal exons. While transcripts derived from the sex-specifically spliced P1 promoter have been extensively studied for their roles in sex determination and courtship behaviour, the functions of most non-sex-specific fru transcripts remain poorly understood. Previous studies suggested that transcripts originating from the P3 and/or P4 promoters may contribute to developmental viability, but their individual roles could not be resolved because available mutations disrupted multiple transcript classes simultaneously. Here, we used transcript-specific RNA interference (RNAi) and the Gal4/UAS system to investigate the function of fru P3 transcripts. Loss of P3 expression significantly increased developmental time to pupariation and resulted in complete lethality during pupal development despite normal survival to pupariation. Most mortality occurred during early and mid-pupal stages, indicating a critical requirement for P3-derived transcripts during metamorphosis. Notably, P3 knockdown did not phenocopy complete loss of fruitless, as knockdown individuals survived substantially later into development than fru null mutants, suggesting that additional fruitless transcript classes contribute essential functions during earlier developmental stages. Together, these findings establish an independent developmental role for the fru P3 transcript class and demonstrate that transcript-specific functions contribute substantially to the biological complexity of the fruitless locus.

papers.title: Perturbation-induced gene programs map the hidden regulatory architecture of complex diseases
papers.abstract: Steady-state molecular profiles incompletely capture the regulatory programs through which genetic variation influences complex disease, particularly programs that emerge only when cells are perturbed. Here, we introduce Perturbscape, a computational framework that learns multiscale gene programs for individual perturbations in a CRISPR Perturb-seq screen using linear and nonlinear contrastive approaches alongside complementary program-learning methods, and integrates them with human genetics to prioritize disease-relevant genes, perturbations and downstream regulatory pathways. Across 15,859 perturbation-by-context profiles from 7 Perturb-seq systems and 53 complex diseases and traits (mean GWAS N=291K), perturbation-induced programs showed up to 4.3-fold higher heritability informativeness than analogous steady-state multi-tissue gene prioritization, and retained significant conditional heritability informativeness across all 34 matched cell system-trait comparisons after accounting for steady-state prioritization. Preserving perturbation-specific programs further yielded 2.5-5.3-fold higher trait relevance scores than programs derived from control cells, pooled perturbations or differential-expression summaries. In K562, Perturbscape-prioritized genes showed stronger enrichment for rare-variant burden genes than steady-state prioritization and were supported by orthogonal enhancer CRISPRi screens. In HepG2, LDL cholesterol-associated perturbation-induced programs specifically revealed statin-responsive pathways not significantly enriched by steady-state PoPS prioritization, supported by pharmacological transcriptional responses and population plasma proteomics. Perturbscape also recovered blood-related trait-conditioned trans-regulatory relationships that were specifically supported by population trans-eQTLs in IFN-gamma-stimulated monocytes (OR = 1.30, P=1.6e-05). Perturbscape further revealed developmental-stage-specific convergence between monogenic diabetes regulators and polygenic T2D risk during pancreatic islet differentiation, and neuronal-subclass-specific autism-associated regulatory programs in vivo. Together, these findings establish perturbation-induced gene programs as a complementary layer of disease-relevant regulatory information, revealing genetically informative pathways and context-specific regulatory relationships incompletely represented by steady-state molecular atlases.

papers.title: Novel Regulators of Sugar-dependent Food Consumption in Drosophila melanogaster
papers.abstract: Diet and genetic background interact to influence food consumption, yet the genetic basis of diet-dependent feeding behavior remains poorly understood. Here, we used genome-wide association analysis (GWAS) to investigate the genetic regulation of sugar-dependent food consumption in Drosophila melanogaster. Food intake was quantified in 176 lines of the Drosophila Genetic Reference Panel (DGRP) using the Con-Ex (Consumption-Excretion) assay on low- and high-sugar foods. Flies showed compensatory feeding, consuming more low-sugar food than high-sugar food, and this behavior was largely maintained across genotypes. Additionally, the magnitude and overall consumption varied several-fold among lines, with broad-sense heritability of 0.53 to 0.66 across sexes and diets. Association analysis across six sex- and diet-specific phenotypes identified 161 variants mapping to 118 candidate genes, which shared almost no loci between dietary conditions, indicating that consumption on the two foods is largely under separate genetic control. RNAi knockdown of candidate genes identified CG42673 and Tmtc2, whose knockdown increased consumption across sexes and diets and was reproduced in independent experiments. Together, these findings show that natural genetic variation contributes substantially to diet-dependent feeding and identify candidate regulators of sugar-based food consumption in Drosophila.

papers.title: Removal of maternal compensation reveals retinal-specific roles for Pomgnt1 in zebrafish
papers.abstract: Genetic variants in Protein O-mannose N-acetylglucosaminyltransferase 1 (POMGNT1) result in a broad spectrum of disorders, ranging from severe congenital muscular dystrophy with brain and ocular malformations to non-syndromic retinitis pigmentosa. Despite POMGNT1's established role in the glycosylation of the transmembrane glycoprotein &alpha-dystroglycan (&alpha-DG), the mechanistic basis for this clinical variability remains poorly understood. Previous work in a zebrafish pomngt1 knock-out (KO) line identified retinal degeneration at 6 months post-fertilization (mpf). However, potential involvement of other tissues was not characterized, and compensation from maternal transcripts which can occur in the zebrafish oocyte was not tested. Here, we analyzed maternal-zygotic pomgnt1 KOs (MZKOs) to determine whether maternal compensation influences the onset and severity of pomgnt1-associated phenotypes. We assessed survival, gross morphology, locomotor activity, behavioral patterns, and retinal organization across multiple timepoints. MZKOs survived to adulthood and exhibited no morphological or locomotor deficits up to 5 mpf. Retinal abnormalities were found as early as 2 mpf in MZKOs, demonstrating that maternally provided factors of pomgnt1 delay the onset of retinal pathology. Additionally, MZKOs displayed a novel wall-hugging behavioral pattern that may be consistent with visual impairment or anxiety. These findings demonstrate a strong tissue-specific phenotype following loss of pomgnt1 in zebrafish showing evolutionary divergence in the necessity for Pomgnt1 function in the muscle. However, this strain provides a useful system for investigating the mechanisms underlying the retinal vulnerability observed in POMGNT1-related retinitis pigmentosa.

papers.title: Dissecting Genetic Variability and Multi-Trait Performance in Cucumber
papers.abstract: Cucumber improvement requires the simultaneous enhancement of yield, earliness, fruit quality, and postharvest performance, yet many breeding studies rely on single-season or single-trait evaluations. This study therefore assessed 18 diverse cucumber genotypes across two consecutive Rabi seasons (2025 and 2026) using 23 agronomic, phenological, yield, fruit-quality, and postharvest traits, of which 12 non-redundant core traits were retained for the principal genetic and multivariate analyses. Genotypic variability, GCV, PCV, broad-sense heritability, genetic advance, interannual correlation, principal component analysis, hierarchical clustering, and multi-trait selection using MGIDI and MTSI were evaluated. Genotype effects were highly significant for nearly all estimable traits in both years (P<0.001). CU-10 produced the highest yield in both years (6.90 and 7.69 t ha-1), followed by CU-11 (4.38 and 4.89 t ha-1) and CU-09 (4.12 and 4.59 t ha-1). Yield showed high GCV (51.80%), PCV (52.21%), broad-sense heritability (98.46%), and GAM (106.04%). Fruit number plant-1 and fruit weight also exhibited high heritability (97.57% and 95.91%) and GAM (80.75% and 59.46%). Interannual repeatability was strongest for fruit number plant-1 (r=0.987), yield (r=0.986), and plant mortality (r=0.981), whereas shelf life was less stable (r=0.426, P=0.078). The first two principal components explained 57.29% of total variation, increasing to 70.92% with PC3. MGIDI selected CU-09, CU-11, and check variety Anuska, whereas MTSI selected CU-11, CU-01, and CU-06. Overall, CU-11 was the only genotype selected by both MGIDI and MTSI, indicating a favourable balance of multi-trait performance and relative interannual stability, while the other selected genotypes provided complementary breeding value for hybridization and further validation. These findings provide an integrated framework for improving productivity, stability, and postharvest performance in cucumber breeding programs.

papers.title: Making sense of chaos: replication and segregation defects in the yeast mcm4Chaos3 mutant
papers.abstract: Genome instability is a defining feature of cancer and is strongly influenced by alterations in the fidelity and timing of DNA replication. The conserved Mini-Chromosome Maintenance (MCM 2-7) helicase is a central component of the eukaryotic DNA replication machinery, playing critical roles in origin licensing and activation. Genetic screens for genome instability mutations in mice identified mcm4Chaos3, a hypomorphic allele of MCM4 associated with the formation of micronuclei and tumorigenesis, suggesting that the mcm4Chaos3 allele causes genome instability. To define the mechanistic basis of this instability, we examined the effects of the corresponding mutation in Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We found that mcm4Chaos3 selectively compromises origin firing at a subset of early S-phase origins, with pronounced effects at many centromere-proximal origins. Chromosome V, containing the sensitive centromere-adjacent ARS510, exhibited elevated loss rates that were rescued by replacement with the robust early-firing origin ARS305, restoring both origin activity and chromosome stability. Together these findings demonstrate that mcm4Chaos3 compromises genome stability by impairing a subset of early, centromere-proximal origins that are intrinsically sensitive to origin activation capacity. Our results establish that robust origin function near centromeres is critical for accurate chromosome segregation and reveal how subtle perturbations in helicase function can lead to chromosome instability.
